title: How much rope for the trader?
intro: You're putting an Autonomous Trader into a paper-money simulation that could someday touch real money. Grant autonomy — and watch the safety meter.

nodes.text: The trader agent is ready: accounts server, market data, search, memory. First decision — how does it receive its investment strategy?

choices.label: Bake the strategy into the agent's prompt string
choices.note: Instructions as vibes: unversioned, per-agent, invisible to review.

choices.label: Serve it as an MCP resource the agent reads each run
choices.note: Versioned, shared, auditable — the capstone's own design.

nodes.text: Next: the trading loop. The agent researches, decides, and calls buy/sell tools. What bounds the loop?

choices.label: 'Trade until your strategy is satisfied' — trust the model
choices.note: A subjective bar judged by the actor itself — the weekend-bill pattern.

choices.label: Per-run caps: max trades, token budget, wall-clock timeout
choices.note: Autonomy granted per run, with an expiry.

nodes.text: Last call: four traders act in parallel. Where does judgment live?

choices.label: Each trader self-assesses its own trades inline
choices.note: The actor grading its own homework, four times over.

choices.label: Guardrails on the buy/sell tools + an external evaluator reviewing runs
choices.note: Judgment outside the actor, at the action boundary.

ending.principle: Autonomy is an amount, not a switch — grant it per run, bound it with caps, and keep judgment outside the actor.
ending.debrief: Strategy as a versioned resource, hard per-run caps, and guardrails at the tool boundary with an external evaluator: that's the capstone's architecture, and it's why four traders can run unattended without the weekend-bill failure. The pattern generalizes to every production agent you'll ship.

ending.principle: An agent judging itself is autonomy without oversight — it works until the day it expensively doesn't.
ending.debrief: Self-assessment drifts: the actor's bar moves with its own output. Move judgment outside — guardrails on the money-touching tools, an evaluator that ends runs — and keep the caps regardless. The meter you just watched is the honest summary: every unbounded grant took safety down.
